title: ZIA Insights: the Admin Console's traffic charts, log viewer and dashboards

prose.label: Where to look.
prose.text: Insights charts a traffic family ([[zia.insights.data-types]]); the Logs tab lists the transactions ([[zia.insights.logs]]), and what a record's fields mean is per family: [[zia.logs.web-records]], [[zia.logs.firewall-records]], [[zia.logs.dns-outcome]], [[zia.logs.tunnel-records]], [[zia.casb.insights-logs]]. Dashboards and widgets: [[zia.insights.dashboards]]. Streaming the same logs out: [[zia.logs.nss-feed-format]]. Retention and consolidation latency: [[shared.log-correlation.streams:zia-retention]]. The Cloud Connector counterpart is [[cloud-connector.insights.analytics]].

prose.label: Open.
prose.text: Whether the chart data is reachable through an API is open {{gap:insights-api}}.

checks.do: Which Insights page a question belongs to, remembering that Threat Insights is described as different from the other Insights pages.
Whether an analysis of a dashboard or report chart can continue to individual transactions through Analyze Chart.

traffic-types.statement: The Insights pages chart each transaction processed by Zscaler on a chart type of the admin's choice and drill down through filters and operators, for Web, Mobile, Firewall, DNS, Tunnel, Threat (which the page calls different from the other Insights pages), SaaS Security, Endpoint DLP, Email DLP and Extranet traffic.

quotes: View insights for each transaction processed by Zscaler on any chart type of your choice.
Quickly drill down on insights with the help of multiple filters and operators available.
Web - Mobile - Firewall - DNS - Tunnel - Threat (different from the other Insights pages) - SaaS Security - Endpoint Data Loss Prevention (DLP) - Email DLP - Extranet

support-tunnel-view.statement: Zscaler Support can view Tunnel Insights even if remote assistance is disabled; the Insights and the Insights Logs articles both say so.

quotes: Zscaler Support can view Tunnel Insights even if remote assistance is disabled.
Zscaler Support can view Tunnel Insights even if Remote Assistance is disabled.

analyze-chart.statement: Analyze Chart on a dashboard or report chart opens it on an Insights page for drill-down to individual transactions; an analysis can also start from the Logs tab of any Insights page.

quotes: To get more information about a chart in a dashboard or report, click an item on the chart and click Analyze Chart.
The chart is displayed in an Insights page where you can interactively drill down to specific transactions.
Alternatively, you can start an analysis by going to the Logs tab of any Insights page.

threat-insights.statement: Threat Insights (Cyberthreat Protection > Insights > Threat Insights) shows organization-specific threats as paths from origins to targets on a 2D map or a 3D globe, with top threat names, categories, origins and targets that can be sorted by trending, severity or volume.

quotes: The Threat Insights page allows you to visually see organization-specific threats in the form of paths from origins to targets.
You can choose to view threat statistics in a 2D map or a 3D globe.
On the Threat Insights page (Cyberthreat Protection > Insights > Threat Insights)
Sort By: Sort the threat statistics by trending, severity, or volume.
Threat Names: View the top threats, according to how you choose to sort.
Threat Categories: View the top threat categories, according to how you choose to sort.
Threat Origins: View the top locations where threats originated from, according to how you choose to sort.
Threat Targets: View the top locations where threats are targeted to, according to how you choose to sort.

insights-api.title: Whether the Insights chart data has an API
insights-api.detail: The Insights pages, dashboards and widgets are console features, and the help articles read for this subject name no API for them. No OneAPI endpoint was looked for. The Z-Insights GraphQL API in shared.analytics.graphql may expose chart-equivalent data and is the place to check.
